legend: Let T=(V,E)%%ZSMJ0%% be a tree with n%%ZSMJ1%% vertices and n−1%%ZSMJ2%% edges. Each edge of the tree can be assigned a colour from {0,1,…,K−1}%%ZSMJ3%%.

A simple path in a tree is called a K%%ZSMJ4%%-rainbow path if all edges along the path of length K%%ZSMJ5%% have distinct colours. An edge is said to be K%%ZSMJ6%%-rainbow-valid if it lies on at least one K%%ZSMJ7%%-rainbow path. A tree is called a K%%ZSMJ8%%-tree if every edge in the tree is K%%ZSMJ9%%-rainbow-valid.

Your task is to assign colours to the edges of a given tree to form a K-tree with the largest possible K%%ZSMJ10%%. For each edge e%%ZSMJ11%%, you must report its assigned colour c(e)∈{0,1,…,K−1}%%ZSMJ12%% and the endpoints of a K-rainbow path that contains e%%ZSMJ13%%.
All indices are zero-based. If multiple valid colourings or paths exist, any may be output.
input: The first line contains a single integer n%%ZSMJ14%% (2≤n≤105)%%ZSMJ15%%. In the next n−1%%ZSMJ16%% lines you are given the edges of the tree. In each of these lines you are given u%%ZSMJ17%% and v%%ZSMJ18%% (0≤u,v≤n−1)%%ZSMJ19%% describing an edge between nodes u%%ZSMJ20%% and v%%ZSMJ21%%.
output: Your output must consist of n%%ZSMJ22%% lines.
In the first line print the maximum possible K%%ZSMJ23%%.

In the next n−1%%ZSMJ24%% lines, each line should contain three integers: c%%ZSMJ25%%, u%%ZSMJ26%% and v%%ZSMJ27%%, where 0≤c≤K−1%%ZSMJ28%% and 0≤u,v≤n−1%%ZSMJ29%%. These integers specify the colour c%%ZSMJ30%% of an edge and the path between u%%ZSMJ31%% and v%%ZSMJ32%%. This path includes the edge e%%ZSMJ33%% and is a K-rainbow. The order of u%%ZSMJ34%% and v%%ZSMJ35%% does not matter.
Edges must be printed in the order they were given in the input.
